company_stages.label: Open-source project listed as a hobby project on dbdb.io
company_stages.summary: PocketBase started in 2022 as an MIT-licensed open source Go project, listed as a hobby project on dbdb.io, with origin listed as Bulgaria. The license explicitly permits offering it as a paid service.

company_stages.label: Seeking grant funding for full-time maintenance
company_stages.summary: The project stopped accepting donations in January 2024 per a community post. Its FLOSS/fund listing later requested a one-time EUR 30,000 for one year of full-time work.

strategy_phases.label: Coordinated launch with rapid release cadence
strategy_phases.summary: Within days of repository creation, v0.1.0 shipped on July 7, 2022, the same day as a Show HN post. A Product Hunt launch followed on July 8, along with many patch releases in the following weeks.

strategy_phases.label: Roadmap-driven product development toward v1
strategy_phases.summary: The project follows a maintainer roadmap and asks contributors to discuss new-feature PRs before opening them. Releases continued through v0.40.4 without backward-compatibility guarantees before v1.0.0. Stated plans include plugins support and a stable v1.

tactics.name: Same-day Show HN with first release
tactics.description: Publish the first tagged release and a Show HN post on the same day, using a one-line positioning statement.
tactics.mechanism: A concrete, downloadable artifact and a crisp tagline give HN readers something to try immediately.

tactics.name: Multi-channel launch week (HN + Product Hunt)
tactics.description: Follow the HN launch with a Product Hunt launch the next day.
tactics.mechanism: It reaches a second audience while initial attention is still high.

tactics.name: Single-file, alternative-to-incumbent positioning
tactics.description: Describe the product as a lightweight single-executable alternative to well-known hosted backends.
tactics.mechanism: A memorable constraint ('1 file') plus comparison to known products (Firebase/Supabase) communicates value instantly. The tagline is reused in community reposts.

tactics.name: Ship fast patch releases after launch
tactics.description: Publish frequent small releases in the weeks after launch.
tactics.mechanism: It shows active maintenance and lets the maintainer quickly fix issues raised by early adopters.

tactics.name: Permissive license that allows third-party hosting
tactics.description: Use the MIT license and explicitly allow the software to be offered as a paid service.
tactics.mechanism: Third parties can build hosting and tooling around the project, extending its reach.

thirty_second.text: PocketBase is an MIT-licensed Go backend that ships as a single executable with an embedded SQLite database, realtime subscriptions, auth and an admin dashboard. It is positioned as a lightweight alternative to Firebase or Supabase. The repository was created on July 5, 2022. The first release and a Show HN post came out on July 7, followed by a Product Hunt launch on July 8. By October 2026 it had about 61,000 stars, 292 releases and 45 contributors. Star growth since launch has come in a series of short bursts that line up in time with large Hacker News posts and GitHub trending placements, with steadier growth between them.

origin.text: PocketBase started in 2022 as an open source Go project with Bulgaria listed as its country of origin. It is listed as a hobby project on dbdb.io. The public repository was created on July 5, 2022, and v0.1.0 was published two days later. The claims do not say why it was built.

first_users.text: The first visible audience came from Hacker News and Product Hunt. A Show HN post on July 7, 2022, the day v0.1.0 shipped, reached 563 points and 111 comments. The next day PocketBase was hunted on Product Hunt by the Product Hunt account and placed #22 with 114 upvotes. It was #1 in Go on GitHub trending from July 9 to 12. The repo gained 7,018 stars between July 7 and July 27, up from roughly zero before. These were most likely developers browsing HN and GitHub, but the claims do not describe who actually adopted it.

flywheel.text: The evidence points to a loop driven by recurring exposure rather than one launch. People other than the maintainer kept reposting PocketBase to Hacker News, often reusing the '1 file' tagline. Two reposts, in January 2024 and November 2025, drew more points than the original Show HN. Over 214 days the repo also returned to GitHub trending, including top-5 placements across all languages in December 2023, April 2025 and July 2025. Star bursts happened around the same time as several of these placements. Separately, a third-party ecosystem grew alongside the project: unofficial hosting (PocketHost), community clients in several languages, and deployment guides. The permissive license allows this kind of outside work. The claims do not measure how much each part feeds the others.

did_differently.text: One reading is that PocketBase competed on simplicity of deployment. It packages the API server, admin dashboard and database into one file and states that constraint plainly in its tagline. It also shipped very quickly after launch: 15 releases between July 7 and July 21, 2022. It keeps a tight scope through a maintainer roadmap, asks contributors to discuss new-feature PRs first, and makes no backward-compatibility guarantee before v1. The single-file design has a known trade-off: it cannot scale horizontally, and one source suggests it suits projects with up to around 10,000 users.

key_takeaways.text: Launch attention came in a tight window. The first release, Show HN and Product Hunt launch happened within two days, and the project reports reaching #1 in Go trending after that. The launch period accounts for the largest star burst in the record, at 7,018 stars in three weeks.

Later growth spikes often line up in time with posts the maintainer did not make. A January 2024 HN repost (630 points) coincided with a 1,387-star burst. The November 2025 repost reached 671 points, more than the original launch post.

A short, concrete description ('backend in 1 file', a Firebase/Supabase alternative) has been reused almost word for word across many HN posts over four years. This suggests the description is easy to repeat.
The permissive license has gone together with outside hosting, community SDKs and deployment guides, which could make adoption easier beyond the official JavaScript and Dart SDKs.

Maintainer-controlled scope is visible in the project's rules. New-feature PRs require prior discussion, and PRs were recently limited to existing collaborators because of LLM spam. Growth has continued under this model, though the claims do not show whether the model caused that growth.
